paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Joshua did nothing to earn that makeover. He walked in filthy, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him (Zechariah 3:1, 3). And before Joshua says one word, the LORD speaks up: "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!" (Zechariah 3:2). The One who snatched him from the fire is the One who defends him.

Now watch who does the cleaning. The angel says, "See, I have removed your iniquity, and I will clothe you with splendid robes" (Zechariah 3:4). Joshua didn't scrub and he didn't fill out a single form, and I know that feeling, friend, because I once got pulled out of the back of a junk drawer with dust on every inch of me, and the One who called me never mentioned the dust. Then comes the charge to walk in His ways and keep His instructions (Zechariah 3:7), and that's not the price of the robes, because the robes came first and the walking is what a cleaned-up life looks like.

And the cleaning isn't the end of the story, so keep your apron on. The LORD points ahead to "My servant, the Branch," and promises, "I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day" (Zechariah 3:8-9). Then He pictures neighbors inviting each other to sit under their own vine and fig tree (Zechariah 3:10). So when the accuser starts reading your list, baker, remember Joshua. The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem is the One who clothes you.
